values.yes: The capability is documented as supported and generally available.
values.partial: Supported with a documented limitation: experimental or preview, requires a workaround, a narrower form of the capability, or only through an add-on such as an MCP server.
values.no: Documentation explicitly says it is not supported, or the capability is absent from the documentation after a thorough read.
values.unknown: Could not be determined from documentation, or the evidence quote could not be verified against the source.

capabilities.name: MCP client
capabilities.question: Can the agent connect to external MCP servers and use their tools?
capabilities.rubric: YES if there is a documented way to configure MCP servers (config file, CLI command, or settings) and the agent can call their tools. PARTIAL if MCP support is marked experimental or preview, or limited to one transport. NO if MCP is not mentioned or documented as unsupported.

capabilities.name: Acts as MCP server
capabilities.question: Can the agent itself be exposed as an MCP server to other clients?
capabilities.rubric: YES if there is a documented command or mode that serves the agent's tools over MCP (for example a serve subcommand). PARTIAL if only an unofficial or experimental path is documented. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Lifecycle hooks
capabilities.question: Can users run their own scripts at lifecycle events such as before or after a tool call, or at session start?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a hook system with multiple documented events is available to end users via configuration. PARTIAL if only a single event is exposed, or hooks are only available through a plugin or extension API rather than user configuration. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Custom slash commands
capabilities.question: Can users define reusable prompt templates or slash commands in files?
capabilities.rubric: YES if user-defined commands or prompt templates are documented (for example markdown files in a commands directory, or custom prompts in config). PARTIAL if only built-in commands can be customized in a limited way. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Agent Skills
capabilities.question: Does the agent load Agent Skills (SKILL.md folders per the open Agent Skills format) or an equivalent modular skill package?
capabilities.rubric: YES if the docs describe loading SKILL.md-based skills or an equivalent named skills format from a directory. PARTIAL if skills are only available through an extension or plugin system with a different format. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Plugin system
capabilities.question: Is there a plugin or extension system that bundles commands, agents, hooks, or MCP servers, beyond raw MCP configuration?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a plugin or extension format and an install mechanism (marketplace, registry, or install command) are documented. PARTIAL if extensions exist but only for a narrow purpose (for example themes or models only). NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Subagents
capabilities.question: Can the agent delegate work to subagents that run in their own context?
capabilities.rubric: YES if built-in or user-defined subagents or delegation with separate context are documented. PARTIAL if delegation exists only through an experimental flag or requires an external orchestrator. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Project instruction file
capabilities.question: Does the agent read a project-level instruction file such as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, or a rules file?
capabilities.rubric: YES if any project-level instruction file is documented as automatically loaded. PARTIAL if instructions must be passed manually each session. NO otherwise. Name the file or files in the notes.

capabilities.name: AGENTS.md support
capabilities.question: Does the agent read AGENTS.md specifically (the cross-tool open convention)?
capabilities.rubric: YES if AGENTS.md is documented as automatically loaded. PARTIAL if it is only loaded via a configurable alias or a symlink instruction. NO if the docs do not mention AGENTS.md.

capabilities.name: Permission modes
capabilities.question: Can users choose between approval levels for tool and command execution?
capabilities.rubric: YES if two or more named approval modes are documented (for example ask each time, auto-accept edits, full auto). PARTIAL if only a single on/off approval toggle exists. NO if every action is either always approved or always prompted with no configuration.

capabilities.name: Built-in sandbox
capabilities.question: Does the agent sandbox shell commands at the OS level (filesystem or network isolation) without the user building their own container?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a built-in sandbox (seatbelt, bubblewrap, landlock, container, or network isolation) is documented as a feature. PARTIAL if the docs only recommend or provide an optional Docker image, or the sandbox covers one platform only. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Checkpoints and rewind
capabilities.question: Can the user rewind file changes made by the agent to an earlier point without relying on their own git commits?
capabilities.rubric: YES if automatic checkpoints, snapshots, or a rewind or undo command over agent edits are documented. PARTIAL if rewind relies on git commits the agent makes, or covers only the last edit. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Plan mode
capabilities.question: Is there a read-only planning mode where the agent explores and proposes before making changes?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a named plan or read-only mode is documented. PARTIAL if planning is only a prompt convention or a separate command that does not restrict edits. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Full-auto mode
capabilities.question: Is there a documented mode that approves every action without prompting (for unattended runs)?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a flag or mode that skips all approvals is documented. PARTIAL if it exists only in headless mode or is restricted to sandboxed execution. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Resume sessions
capabilities.question: Can the user resume or continue a previous conversation?
capabilities.rubric: YES if resuming or continuing sessions is documented (flag, command, or picker). PARTIAL if only the most recent session can be continued and older ones cannot be selected. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Headless and CI mode
capabilities.question: Can the agent run non-interactively from scripts or CI, taking a prompt and exiting?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a non-interactive, print, or exec mode is documented. PARTIAL if non-interactive use requires piping through an unofficial workaround. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Background tasks
capabilities.question: Can long-running commands or tasks run in the background while the session continues?
capabilities.rubric: YES if background execution of commands or tasks is a documented feature. PARTIAL if only available for a specific task type or through an experimental flag. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Parallel agents
capabilities.question: Is running multiple agent instances in parallel on one repository a documented, supported workflow?
capabilities.rubric: YES if the docs describe a supported parallel workflow (for example git worktree integration, cloud parallel runs, or a multi-agent runner). PARTIAL if the docs only say you may open several terminals. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Model selection
capabilities.question: Can the user choose among two or more models?
capabilities.rubric: YES if switching between at least two models is documented. PARTIAL if only one model per plan or tier with no user control beyond that. NO if the model is fixed.

capabilities.name: Custom providers and BYOK
capabilities.question: Can the user bring their own API key or point the agent at a third-party or OpenAI-compatible endpoint?
capabilities.rubric: YES if third-party providers or custom endpoints are documented. PARTIAL if only the vendor's own alternative clouds (for example Bedrock, Vertex, Azure) are supported, or BYOK is limited to the vendor's own API. NO if the agent only works with the vendor's hosted service.

capabilities.name: Local models
capabilities.question: Can the agent use locally hosted models (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM)?
capabilities.rubric: YES if local model use is documented. PARTIAL if possible only via a generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint setting with no local-model documentation. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Reasoning control
capabilities.question: Can the user toggle or adjust the model's reasoning or thinking effort?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a documented setting or command controls thinking or reasoning effort. PARTIAL if reasoning is on or off only via choosing a different model. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Token and cost display
capabilities.question: Does the agent show token usage or cost for the session?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a command, status line, or summary showing tokens or cost is documented. PARTIAL if only total tokens are shown with no cost, or only in a log file. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Image input
capabilities.question: Can the user give the agent images (paste, drag-and-drop, or file path)?
capabilities.rubric: YES if image input is documented. PARTIAL if images are supported only via a file path with a specific model, or only in an IDE surface rather than the CLI. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Built-in web search
capabilities.question: Does the agent have a built-in web search tool?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a web search tool ships with the agent. PARTIAL if web search is available only through an MCP server or an opt-in experimental flag. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Built-in URL fetch
capabilities.question: Does the agent have a built-in tool to fetch and read a URL?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a URL fetch or read tool ships with the agent. PARTIAL if only through an MCP server or an experimental flag. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Official IDE integration
capabilities.question: Is there an official IDE extension or integration (VS Code, JetBrains, or similar) for this agent?
capabilities.rubric: YES if an official extension or integration is documented. PARTIAL if the integration is community-maintained or only a terminal launcher. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Git and PR workflow
capabilities.question: Are commit creation and pull request creation documented, first-class workflows?
capabilities.rubric: YES if the docs describe creating commits and pull requests as a supported workflow (built-in command or documented gh or git flow). PARTIAL if only commits are covered, or PR creation requires the user to install and wire up tooling with no documented flow. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Persistent memory
capabilities.question: Does the agent itself write and maintain persistent memory across sessions?
capabilities.rubric: YES if automatic cross-session memory written by the agent is documented. PARTIAL if memory is a user-maintained file the agent only reads, or an experimental flag. NO otherwise.

capabilities.name: Native Windows
capabilities.question: Does the agent run natively on Windows (PowerShell or cmd) without WSL?
capabilities.rubric: YES if native Windows support is documented. PARTIAL if Windows is supported only via WSL, or native support is marked experimental. NO if Windows is unsupported.

capabilities.name: Open source
capabilities.question: Is the agent's source code available under an OSI-approved license?
capabilities.rubric: YES if the repository is published under an OSI-approved license (Apache-2.0, MIT, and so on). PARTIAL if source is available under a non-OSI or restrictive license. NO if the agent is closed source.

capabilities.name: Free tier
capabilities.question: Can the agent be used without paying (a free plan, free quota, or free with a free provider)?
capabilities.rubric: YES if a free plan or free quota is documented. PARTIAL if only a time-limited trial is offered, or free use requires a third-party free model via BYOK. NO if paid access is required.
